post.caption: Soldiers are named for gold coins. Emperor Constantine made the gold solidus Rome's standard coin. Armies and officials were paid in it. It was struck at 72 to a Roman pound of gold. It kept roughly the same weight for about seven centuries. So soldier comes from Latin solidus, meaning one having pay. The word reached English by about the year 1300. The French sou comes from solidus too. Britain wrote shillings with an s, short for solidus. Until 1971, Britain's pound held 20 shillings.
